findings.title: Password reset link may be built from a caller-supplied Host header
findings.summary: When PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset, the reset email uses the request's Host header as the link origin. Whether an attacker can control that header depends on the production proxy.
findings.suspected_root_cause: build_reset_url falls back to request.host instead of failing when no public origin is configured

trace.note: unauthenticated request names the account to reset
link origin taken from request.host when the setting is empty

evidence.note: PUBLIC_BASE_URL defaults to an empty string
ingress in the repository does not set or restrict Host

blockers: The production proxy configuration is not in the repository, so it is unknown whether an arbitrary Host header reaches the application

resolution.local: Start the app from tests/conftest.py with PUBLIC_BASE_URL unset, post a reset request with a dummy Host, and read the link in the captured outbound mail fixture
resolution.owner_check: Confirm whether the production load balancer forwards the client's Host header unchanged, and whether PUBLIC_BASE_URL is set in the production environment

findings.title: Any tenant can refund another tenant's order
findings.summary: The refund route loads the order by ID and issues the refund without checking that the caller's tenant owns it.
findings.root_cause: POST /orders/{id}/refund is registered without the require_owner dependency that the read and update routes use
findings.violated_invariant: Only the tenant that owns an order may change its payment state
findings.actor: Any authenticated user of any tenant
findings.affected: Orders and payment balances of every other tenant

trace.note: authenticated route; order ID taken from the path
order fetched by ID with no tenant filter
status and balance updated for the fetched order

evidence.note: GET and PATCH routes declare Depends(require_owner); the refund route at line 88 does not

preconditions.detail: A valid session in any tenant
The target order ID is known or guessed; IDs are sequential integers

reproduction.interface: HTTP API through the repository's test client
inputs: POST /orders/1001/refund {"reason": "duplicate"} sent with tenant B's session; order 1001 belongs to tenant A
steps: Load the two-tenant fixture from tests/api/conftest.py
Send the request as the tenant B fixture user
Read order 1001 back as tenant A
reproduction.observed: Response 200; order 1001 status changed to refunded and tenant A's balance was reduced by the order total

fix.strategy: Enforce ownership at the route with the same require_owner dependency the sibling routes use, and add the tenant to the service-layer lookup so the write path cannot be reached with a foreign order
fix.regression_test: tests/api/test_refunds.py: tenant B refunding tenant A's order returns 404 and leaves the order unchanged

changes.change: Fetch the order with get_order_for_tenant(order_id, tenant_id)

likelihood.why: Requires only an ordinary account and a sequential ID

impact.why: Cross-tenant write to payment state was demonstrated

confidence.why: Reproduced locally by the hunter and independently re-read by a verifier

findings.title: Sort parameter interpolated into ORDER BY
findings.summary: The sort value is formatted into the query string, which looked like an injection point.
findings.suspected_root_cause: search_orders builds ORDER BY with string formatting

trace.note: sort taken from the query string

evidence.note: sort is an enum of four column names validated before the handler runs

findings.rejection_reason: The request schema restricts sort to four fixed values, so no caller-controlled text reaches the query
